title: Annotatio III §.VIII: Anathema if bread-substance remains — Pius IV profession/oath names Transsubstantiation
pass_a_gloss: Accordingly, if anyone shall say that in the Most Holy Sacrament of the Eucharist the substance of bread and wine remains together with the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, and shall deny that marvelous and singular Conversion of the whole substance of bread into body and of the whole substance of wine into blood, the species of bread and wine alone remaining, which Conversion the Catholic (Roman) Church most aptly calls Transsubstantiation — let him be Anathema. Nor did they delay the Pope’s definition and the Council’s unjust Confirmation, that profession and oath of faith be made according to this form of Transsubstantiation and no other, and that this one among the new articles of the Roman Symbol be heard under such tenor and frequent penalty: I N. with firm faith believe and profess all and each contained in the symbol of faith which the Holy Roman Church uses; … I likewise profess that in the Mass and in the Sacrament of the Eucharist there is truly, really and substantially the body and blood together with the soul and divinity of our Lord Jesus Christ, and that a conversion is made of the whole substance of bread into body and of the whole substance of wine into Christ’s blood, which Conversion the Catholic (Roman) Church calls Transsubstantiation — see the Bull of Pius IV confirming the Council of Trent on the form of the oath of profession of faith published together with the same Council.
pass_b_english: Anathema if anyone says bread and wine substance remain with body and blood, or denies that singular conversion with species alone remaining.

Nor do they delay the Pope’s definition and the Council’s unjust confirmation: profession and oath must follow this Transsubstantiation form — Ego N. … truly, really, substantially body and blood; conversion of whole substances — Pius IV’s bull on the Trent faith-oath.
source_text: Proinde, si quis dixerit in SSmo. Eucharistiæ Sacramento remanere substantiam panis & vini unà cum corpore & sanguine Domini nostri Jesu Christi, negaveritque mirabilem illam & singularem Conversionem totius substantiæ panis in corpus, & totius substantiæ vini in sanguinem, manentibus duntaxat speciebus panis & vini, quam quidem Conversionem Catholica (Romana) Ecclesia aptissimè Transsubstantiationem appellat, Anathema sit. Nec morati Papæ definitionem, Conciliiq; injustam Confirmationem, ut juxta hanc Transsubstantiationis, non aliam formam, professio & juramentum fidei fiat, utque unus hic è novis Symboli Romani articulis sub tenore & pœna frequenti hujusmodi exaudiatur: Ego N. firma fide credo & profiteor omnia & singula, quæ continentur in symbolo fidei, quo S. Romana Ecclesia utitur; … profiteor pariter in Missa atque in Eucharistiæ Sacramento esse verè realiter & substantialiter corpus & sanguinem unà cum anima & divinitate Domini nostri Jesu Christi, fierique conversionem totius substantiæ panis in corpus & totius substantiæ vini in sanguinem Christi, quam Conversionem Catholica (Romana) Ecclesia Transsubstantiationem appellat: vide Bullam Pii IV. Confirm. Concil. Trident. super forma juramenti professionis fidei unà cum eodem Concilio editam.
